videos.title: ACoC 2025: Day 15: RC Circuits with Voltage Gain
videos.description:
Day 15:  Passive RC circuits can have a transfer function with voltage gain.

This seems rather non-intuitive at first, but it is not even uncommon.  Something like a twin-T network is a fairly classic example. Perhaps it is not as intuitive a topology to introduce the idea with compared to a simple RC ladder...

LR networks can do this too and I think this isn't as surprising as L is associated with induction and transformers.  However even perfectly shielded inductors work, it is just a lot…

videos.title: ACoC 2025: Day 14: Animal Tracking Transmitter / Fox Hunt Beacon
videos.description:
Day 14: A pulsed RF beacon with simple implementation and a long battery life.  It emits a distinctive slightly chirped RF pulse that is otherwise quite stable - the frequency being defined by a quartz crystal.  Duty cycle and output power are easy to adjust and it can operate from single cell voltages down to sub-volt power supplies.

Once upon a time it would have been suitable for tagging animals for scientific field studies.  Now days one would use a more sophisticated device with GPS and…

videos.title: ACoC 2025: Day 13: Forever Flasher Too?
videos.description: Day 13:  Very low power blocking oscillator based LED flasher, powered by a 1.5 volt cell.  It flashes about once every 5 seconds for 35 ms, the inverter oscillates at about 80 kHz.  It will oscillate down to a 500-600 mV supply giving it excellent battery life.

videos.title: ACoC 2025: Day 10: Poisson Process Emulator (aka Geiger Counter Prop)
videos.description: Day 10: A noise source that emulates the Poisson statistics of a Geiger mode radiation rate meter. That is to say a toy noise maker that sounds like a real Geiger counter detecting radiation.  It actually does emulate Poisson statistics fairly well over a reasonable range of rates (basically until the monostable is no longer working properly), with exponentially distributed inter-pulse intervals.

videos.title: #405: Using TinySA Ultra to measure keyer speed of a Kenwood TS-890S transceiver
videos.description:
This video shows how to measure the keyer speed of a CW transmitter using a TinySA Ultra in Zero Span mode with a trigger.  The formulas are simple:
WPM = 1.2/unit_length
and
unit_length = 1.2/WPM
...where: 
   WPM = Words Per Minute
   unit_length = time duration of a "dit" 
The rig is a Kenwood TS-890S, and the measurement verified that the WPM setting is accurate (unlike some rigs shown in my previous video, linked below)

videos.title: ACoC 2025: Day 9: Folded Cascode TIA
videos.description: Day 9: A moderately fast TIA for PD amplification built using a discrete BJT folded cascode topology.  The supply voltage is 3.3 volts and it has 10K of transimpedance, a BPW34 will require about 500 fF to 1 pF of compensation capacitance for best flatness given a reverse bias from the 3.3 volt supply.  Higher transimpedances are possible with resulting loss of bandwidth, and vice versa.  It is DC coupled and inverting, a lot of DC light will saturate it, you can AC couple it to avoid this or…

videos.title: ACoC 2025: Day 8: Dim Bulb Tester
videos.description:
Day 8: A very simple but useful piece of test equipment for mains work.  Basically just a light bulb in series with the active and a switch, it prevents dead shorts across the mains and limits in-rush currents.

Great for bringing up old vacuum tube equipment, reforming electrolytic capacitors, smoke testing new designs, etc.  You can set the maximum current by changing the bulb, I have 25, 100, 200 and 500 watt bulbs for mine.  Use an incandescent lamp, not a modern LED one.  100 watts is a…

videos.title: ACoC 2025: Day 7: Barkhausen Noise
videos.description: Day 7: A demonstration of magnetic Barkhausen noise and some discussion of ways an electric analogue of it may be detectable, likening the technique to that of Partial Discharge testing.

videos.title: ACoC 2025: Day 6: Feedback Microammeter
videos.description:
Day 6: The main benefit of feedback ammeters is elimination of the "burden voltage" seen with shunt ammeters.  Magnetic approaches do not have this problem either, but have limited sensitivity unless they also introduce significant series impedances reflected through the current transformer.

The disadvantages are that the instrument has to source or sink the full measured current.  For lower currents this is not challenging and the main non-idealities remaining are closed loop bandwidth…

videos.title: ACoC 2025: Day 5: Regulated Low-Volt Power Supply
videos.description:
Day 5: A regulated sub-volt power supply for experiments.

A simple linear design, not efficient but easy to implement and low noise.  The intention is to have an "expanded scale" at 100 mV or so for ease of use in a specific application.  It is likely useful for tunnel diode supplies and testing power harvesters of the low-voltage type.  Optional fixed current limiter with only two more components.  Designed to be used with about 5 volts of input voltage, but should work fine on lower voltages…
